payload.claim: write_follow_ups indexes stack.layers[0] and stack.layers[-1] (lines 245-246) before ever calling qualify, so a stack with zero layers raises IndexError instead of the empty-groups result the module's own docs assume. A zero-layer StackReview is a real state: run_end_review (saffron/end_review.py:505-561) always runs a join and a layer pass, and review_joins/review_stack return None/[] whenever no task reached READY_FOR_REVIEW that night (e.g. every task failed or was refused before packaging), producing StackReview(join=None, layers=[]). The spec's own 'undriven' note says 'A stack with no layers. qualify then returns no group,' implying write_follow_ups should just produce zero candidates, but the code never reaches qualify in that case because it crashes first on the empty list. No test in this diff constructs a zero-layer stack (both tests use a two-layer stack), so this boundary case is untested and the crash is invisible to the gates.
